assertion_audit:
Added assertions at the reviewed head, in tests/test_a_plan_review_record_is_decoded_once.py:
62 and 64: fail if either decoded result is absent or differs from the separately serialized pending fixture; 63 positively controls the decoder at one first read; 65 fails with two if the uncached reader is restored, as the retarget control demonstrates.
76: fails if the initial on-disk pending value is not loaded; 77 fails if the initial load performs zero or multiple decodes; 88 checks that the fixture actually rewrites the same inode; 89-91 fails if stale pending content survives the rewrite; 92 fails if invalidation does not decode again or decoding repeats excessively.
109: establishes the stored value is accepted with the original producer digest; 111-114 fails if the reader bypasses producer validation on a cached envelope, returning pending instead of the missing sentinel after the mock digest changes; 115 fails unless both calls check the digest; 116 fails if the payload is decoded twice despite caching.
141 and 146: require nonempty entries on cold and warm reads; 142 positively controls one initial decode; the patch at 143-145 raises if warm code calls deepcopy, with its observed failure in copy-negative-control.log; 147 rejects an extra warm decode; 149-151 rejects stale entries after the store is rewritten; 152 requires one new decode after that rewrite.
160 and 161: fail if immutable conversion changes dict/list type compatibility; the raises context at 162-163 fails if a nested entry can be mutated; 168 and 169 fail if clearing independently returned outer entry/stamp dictionaries erases cached content.
178: fails if changing the index path for the same tree returns an older envelope; the offset is written to disk and independently read, so removing path validation returns the prior offset and reddens this assertion; 179 fails if more than one file revision is retained for that tree.
188: requires each newly created tree to return entries; 189 fails if the count bound does not evict down to two entries; 193 and 194 require the newest tree to remain readable without decoding; 195 and 196 require the evicted oldest tree to decode again. This sequence proves oldest eviction for this access order; it does not independently exercise hit-induced LRU reordering.
205-207: positively controls nonempty payload delivery on both oversized reads; 208 fails if an oversized payload is retained and avoids the second decode; 209 fails if any oversized cache entry remains. The test checks an individually oversized file; aggregate source-byte eviction is additionally read in metadata_index.py:1934-1941 rather than asserted by this test.
234-236: fails if a same-content mtime change loses its discovery state or immutable-entry mutation raises; 237 fails if refreshing the signature mutates the previously returned entry; 238-240 fails if the persisted refreshed signature is not the file's newly observed stat signature.
No added assertion has both sides tied to the same mutable variable. The expected dictionaries are serialized into file bytes before a distinct read, and digest/status, decoder counts, TypeError, rewritten bytes, cache sizes and OS stat identity provide independent observations. The pre-existing record-copy assertion at 51 was only shifted by imports, not added in this delta.
